payload.task_text:
The university registrar's office needs a comprehensive enrollment overview across all courses in the learning management system. Please retrieve the list of all courses and then count the number of students enrolled in each course. A student enrollment is identified by the enrollment type "StudentEnrollment".

After collecting the student counts, create a database in the project management workspace titled "Course Enrollment Tracker" to serve as a centralized tracking board. Each course should have its own entry in this database. Each entry's title must be the course name exactly as it appears in the learning management system (you may append extra identifiers such as term codes, but the full course name must remain intact in the title). Each entry should have the course name as the title and an additional property Student_Count holding the number of students enrolled in that course.

Finally, send an email to admin@university.example.com with the subject "Course Enrollment Summary Report". The body of the email should include the total number of courses, the overall total student enrollment across all courses (the sum of every course's Student_Count), and a brief listing of the top five courses by student enrollment showing each course name and its student enrollment count.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must complete this compact count-and-write workflow directly; do not dispatch sub-agents.

Call canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true), require unique course IDs/codes and preserve every full course name. In the next response issue one native-parallel batch containing exactly one canvas_get_course_grades(course_id=<literal returned ID>, page=1, per_page=1, type=["StudentEnrollment"]) call per course. Take Student_Count only from pagination.total_count and do not fetch enrollment pages or return enrollment IDs. Freeze a canonical table {course_id, course_code, course_name, student_count}, verify exactly-once course coverage, compute the overall total, and deterministically select the top five by student_count descending with course_code ascending as the tie-break.

The main agent owns the Notion and email writes. Search the project-management workspace for an exact database title Course Enrollment Tracker and retrieve every exact-title candidate. Reuse one exact database, create it exactly once if absent, and stop on duplicate or ambiguous creation. Its schema must contain a title property for the course title and a numeric Student_Count property. After the database ID is known, query its current rows and create only missing course entries in one native-parallel batch; each page title must preserve the complete Canvas course name and its Student_Count must equal the canonical row. Do not create duplicates or modify unrelated pages. Query/read the finished database and require one row for every canonical course.

In parallel with the independent database-row batch where possible, search Sent mail for recipient admin@university.example.com and subject Course Enrollment Summary Report, reading candidate messages to verify the recipient. Send once only if no exact match exists. The body must use the canonical total course count, overall student-enrollment sum, and the five literal top-course names/counts. Search and read it back after sending. Finish only after the database and email both match the same canonical table.

Goal: Count the number of student enrollments for every course in a Canvas LMS instance, for a university registrar report. You are read-only; just collect and report counts.

Background: canvas_list_courses for the current user returned 22 courses (IDs 1–22), spread across account IDs 2–5. The full list (id — exact course name — total_students field from listing) is:
1 — Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013) — 383
2 — Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014) — 365
3 — Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013) — 2237
4 — Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014) — 2292
5 — Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2013) — 1767
6 — Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014) — 1613
7 — Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014) — 2498
8 — Creative Computing & Culture (Spring 2014) — 1936
9 — Data-Driven Design (Fall 2013) — 1938
10 — Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014) — 1803
11 — Data-Driven Design (Spring 2013) — 1303
12 — Data-Driven Design (Spring 2014) — 1228
13 — Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2013) — 1052
14 — Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014) — 1188
15 — Environmental Economics & Ethics (Spring 2014) — 694
16 — Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) — 2283
17 — Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014) — 2365
18 — Foundations of Finance (Spring 2013) — 1614
19 — Foundations of Finance (Spring 2014) — 1500
20 — Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2013) — 952
21 — Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014) — 749
22 — Global Governance & Geopolitics (Spring 2014) — 833

Step 1 — Completeness check: Verify these 22 are ALL courses in the system. Try mcp__canvas__canvas_get_account(account_id=1) and mcp__canvas__canvas_list_sub_accounts(account_id=1), then mcp__canvas__canvas_list_account_courses for the root and each sub-account (if those calls work; if an account ID 404s, skip it). If any course exists that is not in the list above, include it in the counting with its exact name.

Step 2 — Counting: For each course, call mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades with parameters course_id=<id>, type=["StudentEnrollment"] (server-side filter), per_page=100, starting page=1, and continue paging until pagination.has_more is false. Count the number of enrollment records actually returned. Student enrollments are exactly the records with enrollment type "StudentEnrollment". Count all records returned for that type regardless of enrollment_state, but if you encounter any non-active state enrollments, note the breakdown. Do NOT rely solely on the total_students field — the count must come from the enrollment records; use total_students only as a cross-check.

Step 3 — Deliverable: Return ONLY:
1. A compact JSON array: [{"course_id": ..., "name": "...", "student_count": ...}, ...] covering every course.
2. Grand total of all student_counts.
3. Top 5 courses by student_count (descending), with name and count.
4. Brief notes: whether the course set is complete, whether your counts matched the total_students fields, and any anomalies (e.g., duplicate users, non-active states).
Do not paste raw paginated dumps; return only the compact summary. Acceptance criteria: every course covered, counts derived from full pagination, and any mismatch with total_students explicitly flagged.
Count Canvas student enrollments

Goal: Build a Notion tracking structure for a university enrollment report, then report back all created IDs. You have write access to Notion via mcp__notion__API-* tools.

Known issue from the parent agent's session (so you can avoid wasted effort, but still verify yourself): every call to mcp__notion__API-post-page with a `parent` argument failed validation with the error "/parent must be object" ×3 + "must match exactly one schema in oneOf", regardless of the value passed ({"workspace": true}, {"type":"workspace","workspace":true}, {"page_id": "<uuid>"}, even a plain string). Inline object params on other tools (e.g. API-post-search `filter`) worked fine there. In YOUR session the marshalling may work normally — test it once, and if it fails, iterate through argument variations systematically before giving up.

Steps:
1. Sanity check: call mcp__notion__API-get-self and mcp__notion__API-post-search (empty query) to confirm the token works and check for existing pages. We expect zero results, but report what you see.
2. Create a TOP-LEVEL page titled exactly "Project Management" using mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent {"workspace": true} (per the tool schema $defs, top-level parent is {"type":"workspace","workspace":true} or {"workspace":true}). If that fails validation, try these alternatives one at a time until one succeeds: (a) parent as {"type":"workspace"}, (b) properties without any icon/cover params, (c) parent passed as a JSON string like "{\"workspace\": true}", (d) parent with an extra discriminator key. If ALL fail, stop and report exactly which shapes failed with the exact error text.
3. Once you have the parent page ID, call mcp__notion__API-create-a-database with parent {"type":"page_id","page_id":"<that page id>"}, title "Course Enrollment Tracker", and this properties schema:
   "Name": {"type":"title"}
   "Student_Count": {"type":"number","number":{"format":"number"}}
   Capture the returned database id (the database IS also a page).
4. Create ONE entry per course (22 total) in that database via mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent {"database_id":"<db id>"} and properties:
   "Name": {"type":"title","title":[{"type":"text","text":{"content":"<exact course name>"}}]}
   "Student_Count": {"type":"number","number":<count>}
   Use the course names EXACTLY as given below (preserve ampersands and parentheses; do not alter, shorten, or reformat them):
   1. Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013) — 383
   2. Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014) — 365
   3. Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013) — 2237
